title: Why a positive test can mean only 9%

frames.caption: 1,000 people. The disease affects 1 in 1,000 of them, and the test is 99% accurate both ways: it catches 99% of sick people and clears 99% of healthy ones.
On average just 1 of them is sick (orange). Easy to miss.
Test everyone. The sick person tests positive (green). But 1% of the 999 healthy people also test positive: about 10 false positives (red).

You tested positive, so you are one of the 11 highlighted people. Only 1 of them is sick: 9%. That matches Bayes' theorem exactly (9.0%). The test is excellent; the disease is just so rare that healthy people's 1% error rate outnumbers the sick.

A second, independent positive test changes everything: now the starting population is these 11 people, 1 in 11 sick, and the same calculation gives 91%. Bayes in action: yesterday's posterior is today's prior.
